clue.text: One bit of European cash invested in squalid area — age required

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: a run-down, squalid district
one as the indefinite article
the European Currency Unit, forerunner of the euro

explanation.surface: A euro coin has been sunk into some slum district, and an era is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: The ECU, the European Currency Unit, was the euro's forerunner, so it is a fair 'bit of European cash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saeculum is Latin for a generation or lifetime, an extended period of time or epoch.

clue.text: Old Yemenis mostly cast down from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom up runs the letters backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to abase is to humble or bring low

explanation.surface: Ancient Arabians, largely downcast, are seen from underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Saba, biblical Sheba, was the ancient kingdom and people of south-west Arabia, modern Yemen.

clue.text: Examining cloth in maturity coating bone

indicators.note: a coating wraps round something, so the first word's letters enclose the next

parts.note: coming of age is reaching maturity
a forearm bone

explanation.surface: Inspecting fabric in old age as it wraps an aching bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aulnage was the official measurement and inspection of woollen cloth, done by an alnager.

clue.text: Pa disturbed with extra noise — it's infuriating

definitions.note: read as a verbal noun, the act of infuriating

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Father is bothered by more din, and it is driving him mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperation is the state or act of provoking great annoyance, so it stands for infuriating as a noun.

clue.text: Most of decree taken up in textual emendation

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking letters up reads them from bottom to top
most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an official order

explanation.surface: An editor changes a text, raising most of a royal order.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers marks this Shakespearean word as an editors' emendation, a conjectured reading for decide, so the label itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records the form only as a conjectured editorial correction in a Shakespeare text, short for decide.

clue.text: Boil rind up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from the bottom

parts.note: the skin of fruit

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: simmer the peel to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Leep is a dialect verb meaning to boil or parboil, found in Chambers.

clue.text: Seine calm originally? It may result in a trip

definitions.text: It may result in a trip

indicators.note: the question suggests the letters were once in a different order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A calm Seine at the start might lead to a pleasant boat outing in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' suggests a journey along the river; it is a drug-induced hallucinatory experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescaline, the hallucinogen from peyote, induces visions, which slang calls a trip.

clue.text: Scriptural academic opening mouth causes dispute

indicators.note: something opening a mouth goes into it, so these letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: Latin for mouth, used in anatomy
Doctor of Divinity, a scholar of scripture

explanation.surface: A biblical scholar who speaks up sparks an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' reads as a verb on 'mouth' but places the scholar inside it. Chambers gives odds as a noun for quarrel, as in being at odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at odds means quarrelling, and Chambers gives odds itself as a noun for strife or variance.

clue.text: Swinging to and fro

parts.note: surface reading: a plain description of something moving back and forth; setter's reading: a reduplicated jingle word for dangling loosely, of the kind built by vowel change

explanation.walkthrough: A plain definition with no wordplay, as Azed sometimes allows for a long answer; the reduplicated form echoes see-saw and ding-dong.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingle-dangle describes something hanging loosely and swaying back and forth, as an adjective or adverb.

clue.text: Tropical fish making whoopee at bottom of tub!

indicators.note: in a down entry, the bottom comes last, so this piece follows the next

parts.note: a dan is a small tub or barrel, used in mining
io is a cry of joy or triumph

explanation.surface: An aquarium fish frolics in the bottom of the bathtub.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are Chambers rarities: a dan is a mining tub, io a shout of exultation.
explanation.definitionFit: The danio is a small, often striped freshwater fish of tropical Asia, popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Take a quick look at ribbons for underwear

parts.note: to scan is to glance over
ties are strips of ribbon for fastening

explanation.surface: Someone glances at the ribbons on display in a lingerie shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanties is a colloquial word for skimpy knickers or women's briefs.

clue.text: What'll promote plant growth wife's sown in middle of rains

indicators.note: seed sown in soil goes inside it, so these letters go within the next ones
the central part of the word is kept and its ends dropped

parts.note: the inner three letters of the word
short for Latin uxor, wife, as in legal documents

explanation.surface: A gardener's note: the wife has sown seed mid-downpour to help plants grow.
explanation.walkthrough: UX, short for uxor, is the wife found in wills and legal Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An auxin is a plant hormone that stimulates growth by cell elongation in shoots and roots.

clue.text: Glee I wasted on account being mournful

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Someone whose cheer was squandered on an account is now sorrowful.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead, so sad and plaintive.

clue.text: Means of climbing within beans twined round pole for leguminous shrub (12, two words)

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the rearranged letters that follow
twining twists strands together, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: something you climb with rungs
taken as written for rearranging
north pole, abbreviated N

explanation.surface: Runner beans have twined round a pole and up a ladder in the vegetable garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twined round pole' tempts you to put the beans round N, but N joins the beans in the rearrangement, which then wraps the climbing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladder senna is a pea-family shrub, Colutea, named for its inflated papery seed pods.

clue.text: Member of the lower orders sips boozily in anticipation

parts.note: a proletarian, a working-class person

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A worker drinks tipsily, looking forward to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolepsis is the rhetorical device of anticipating an objection or treating a future event as already done.

clue.text: Sentimentality with line as in Jock's bloomer

parts.note: sickly sentiment is goo
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A Scot's blunder is soppy, with a line drawn under it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; it is a flower, and Jock marks the word as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Gool is a Scots name for the corn marigold, a yellow flowering plant of cornfields.

clue.text: Opposed to liquor being offered by adult

a spirit

explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect or colloquial form of against, meaning hostile or in opposition to.

clue.text: Hard stuff that splits à la copper when treated

parts.note: taken as written, accent dropped, for rearranging

explanation.surface: Some hard metal cracks apart, like copper does once processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' suggests strong drink or metal; here it is a mineral fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper coal is a lignite that splits into thin, leaf-like sheets, a hard fuel that cleaves.

clue.text: Asian fur transformed poky inns

indicators.note: something transformed has changed shape, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Cramped hostelries have been made over with luxurious fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponyskin is the pelt of a foal or pony, often from central Asian breeds, used like fur.

clue.text: Stunner, forward — one's for the plucking

parts.note: a knockout, which stuns a boxer
as in pushing a door to, moving it forward to shut

explanation.surface: A dazzling forward player is a prize waiting to be picked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the plucking' suggests something ripe for taking; it describes how the instrument is played.
explanation.definitionFit: The koto is a long Japanese zither whose strings the player plucks with picks.

clue.text: Bone fed to it cheers fighting dog

indicators.note: food fed to something goes into it, so these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
Latin for bone, used in anatomy

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a bone to their combative hound with a cheery word.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is everyday British for thanks, as is ta.
explanation.definitionFit: The tosa is a large Japanese mastiff breed developed for dogfighting.

clue.text: What may distinguish legionnaire exchanging parts of spear

indicators.note: the word's two halves swap places, so its end moves to the front

parts.note: a long-shafted infantry spear

explanation.surface: A Roman legion soldier is swapping bits of his spear for another weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legionnaire' summons Rome, but this is the French Foreign Legion and its flat-topped cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The kepi, a peaked flat-topped cap, is the famous emblem of the French Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Author experiences thoughts

parts.note: a pen writes, and pen can stand for the writer
to see is to experience, as in seen better days

explanation.surface: A writer goes through things in life.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is French; Pascal's Pensées are his collected thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensées are thoughts or reflections set down in writing, as a literary form.

clue.text: One with few positive qualities making appearance in dinner- dance

indicators.note: the answer turns up inside the words that follow, spanning the hyphen

parts.note: letters running across the two parts

explanation.surface: A dull guest turns up at a formal dinner with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is a socially inept, boring person, someone thought to have little charm or appeal.

clue.text: I'll be appearing in former rank

indicators.note: a performer appearing in a show is inside it, so this letter goes within the next word

parts.note: old means former, as in an old boss
the pronoun itself, the will being future tense

explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like military grade; it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare word for smelling strongly and offensively, the same sense as rank.

clue.text: In Shakespeare, mean old fellow switching parts

explanation.walkthrough: 'switching parts' suggests an actor's roles; here it moves the halves of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vilde is a Shakespearean spelling of vild, itself a form of vile, meaning base or mean.

clue.text: They begged for their food etc, form of boniness gripping one

clue.text: Old time model, centre of fashion

love is zero in tennis

clue.text: Dirk, maybe? Or Brannagh, in short on the up?

explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade, so a dirk is one example of the same weapon type.

clue.text: Antelope jumping almost perkily around season
